# I stopped running after ten years

From the spring I turned thirty-two, I got up at 5:30 every morning and ran five kilometres. I ran in the rain, and I ran laps around hotels on business trips. Last winter I stopped.

It was my knee. My right knee hurt every time I went down stairs, and the orthopaedist said the meniscus was wearing thin. If I wanted to keep running, he said, three times a week at most. I could have kept going three times a week. I quit instead. Running every morning had become a rule, and I think I felt that one morning off would break the whole rule.

I started walking the dog for forty minutes in the evening instead. The first week felt like nothing: I didn't get out of breath and I didn't sweat. Somewhere in the second week I noticed my head was quieter on those walks than it had ever been on a run. When I ran, I thought about pace and distance the whole time.

So it seems what I liked was not running but half an hour of not having to talk to anyone. The morning run used to be that half hour. Now the evening walk is, and it lasts forty minutes.

My knee still aches a little. In spring I might try running again, twice a week and short distances to begin with. Not as a rule this time; only on the mornings I feel like it.
